thread.title: Apple's iPhone Demand 'Lukewarm,' Says Longbow; Morgan Stanley Stays Bullish

author: Barron's
title: Apple's iPhone Demand 'Lukewarm,' Says Longbow; Morgan Stanley Stays Bullish
text:
Apple ( AAPL ) shares are down 48 cents, at $175.71, amidst dueling research reports from Longbow Research and Morgan Stanley , which take differing views on how the company's iPhone is faring this season.
Longbow's Shawn Harrison cuts his rating on Apple to Neutral from Buy, writing that given a "lackluster" reception to the iPhone 8, he now anticipates "only a good, not great iPhone cycle" for the fiscal year ending in September.
Sales of all models may rise only 7.5% this year, to 233 million, versus the 11% growth the Street is expecting writes Harrison, and down from what he had originally thought might be 14.5% growth, to 248 million units.
Harrison cites unidentified "contacts" offering production estimates for iPhone that are below what was originally expected for Q1 and Q2 of this fiscal year - the December and March quarters:
Contacts saw double-digit year over year CY4Q iPhone production growth, but now see a downtick to +2-4% CY1Q growth. Sales of AAPL's Taiwanese suppliers increased 16% year over year for CY4Q. Previously contacts were noting mid-single-digit CY4Q growth and the potential for double-digit plus CY1Q growth. CY4Q iPhone production beat prior forecasts on easing supply constraints and stronger demand for older models, which should aid our view of better than consensus FY1Q/CY4Q AAPL iPhone shipments. Yet, due to lackluster iPhone 8 demand and the high price of the iPhone X blunting some consumer interest, contacts now see CY1Q/FY2Q production up only low-single digits. We still see a better than seasonal March quarter for suppliers given the late iPhone X launch, but with a lower kicker.
In contrast, Morgan Stanley's Katy Huberty reiterates an Overweight rating, and a $200 price target, writing that China continues to be a bright spot for Apple.
Huberty has no concerns about iPhone X stealing away demand from iPhone 8:
AlphaWise data shows iPhone X adoption outpacing iPhone 8/8+ as Apple retention and switching rates dwarf Chinese competitors. Plus, an increasing mix of upgrades from the much larger base of 3+ year old iPhones points to a strong upgrade cycle in China. The 4 week period ending December 17th marked the 2nd 4-week period with a full 28 days of iPhone X data, and Apple's retention rate continues to climb faster than competitors.
